title: DOM traversal and mutation
learningObjectives: Explain dom traversal and mutation and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: The DOM represents a document as a tree of nodes. JavaScript can traverse it with parentElement, children, closest(), querySelector(), and related APIs. It can mutate nodes using append, prepend, remove, replaceWith, and textContent.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding the tree helps select the right node and avoid brittle selectors. Prefer semantic structure and safe text insertion when rendering dynamic data.
understand.analogy: The DOM is a family tree of elements; traversal moves between parents, children, and nearby relatives.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: The code locates a nested heading, finds its nearest section, creates a paragraph, and appends text without parsing HTML.

examples.explanation: The code locates a nested heading, finds its nearest section, creates a paragraph, and appends text without parsing HTML.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Build a card with nested elements. Traverse from a button to its card and update a status paragraph safely.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: Which method finds the nearest ancestor matching a selector, including the element itself?
questions.explanation: closest walks from the element through its ancestors and returns the first matching element.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach when using browser APIs?
options: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.answer: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.explanation: Browser features need graceful fallback, privacy-aware permission, and lifecycle management.
